walkthrough:
Express $x^2$ as a function of $y$ along the curve $y = \frac{6}{x}$:
$$x = \frac{6}{y} \implies x^2 = \frac{36}{y^2}$$

Set up the definite integral for the volume generated by revolving the region between the curve and $x = 1$ around the $y$-axis from $y = 2$ to $y = 6$:
$$V = \pi \int_2^6 \left(x_{\text{curve}}^2 - x_{\text{line}}^2\right) dy = \pi \int_2^6 \left(\frac{36}{y^2} - 1^2\right) dy$$

Differentiate the curve equation with respect to $x$:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = -6x^{-2} = -\frac{6}{x^2}$$

Set the gradient equal to the slope of the line $y + 2x = 0$ ($m = -2$):
$$-\frac{6}{x^2} = -2 \implies 2x^2 = 6 \implies x^2 = 3$$
Since $x > 0$, we have $x = \sqrt{3}$.

Verify that point $X(\sqrt{3}, 2\sqrt{3})$ lies on the line $y = 2x$:
$$y = 2(\sqrt{3}) = 2x$$
Thus, point $X$ lies on the line $y = 2x$.
